newsitem.title: INDIA: India raises limit on foreign equity shareholding.
newsitem.headline: India raises limit on foreign equity shareholding.

text.p: India is raising the limit on the stake that foreign direct investors can hold in non-core, non-strategic industries to 74 percent, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Thursday.

"We are raising the limit (on foreign direct investment) up to 74 percent for non-core, non-strategic industry," he told a conference organised by Euromoney publications. At present, the limit is 51 percent.
Chidambaram said the limit on foreign equity in core sector industries remained at 49 percent.
Earlier this week the Industry Ministry proposed widening the range of industries that can receive automatic approval for 51 percent ownership.
The ministry had also proposed establishing another list of industries in which foreign investors could take up to a 74 percent stake with automatic government approval.
